profile.intro: A theatre maker, director and performer working on the relationship between the human body and objects as agents in their own right. Trained first in physics and then in theatre directing, his work began in puppet and object theatre, moved toward new-materialist practice, and now turns on questions of consciousness, the senses, non-human beings and artificial intelligence.

statement:
My work has always lived between two worlds. One is scientific thinking: an interest in matter, the cosmos and structure. The other is artistic practice: the body, the senses, images, improvisation and community.

Through yoga, kalaripayattu, movement meditation and improvisation I came to understand the body not as a tool of expression but as an instrument for asking questions. So for me a performance is less about what to show than about how to share my encounter with the world with others. In that sharing, bodies and objects act as equals.

Good art becomes possible when there is a good life, and I believe good art can lead toward a good life.

phases.name: Yosup
phases.subtitle: An individual asking questions through the body
phases.text: Physics taught him to see the world as matter, force, relation and motion. Theatre showed him how the body senses, remembers and meets others.

phases.name: Performance Group Tuida
phases.subtitle: Open theatre, nature-friendly theatre, moving theatre
phases.text: With performance group Tuida (Korean for “to run, to leap, the heart beats”) he built a polyphonic stage language of bodies, objects, puppets, masks and live music. In 2010 the group moved to a closed rural school in Hwacheon and founded Tutbat Arts Farm, folding daily life into creation. Its final period turned toward theatre as testimony to historical pain.

phases.name: Research Collective Muddha
phases.subtitle: A research platform on consciousness, senses, matter and the non-human
phases.text: Muddha (묻다, “to ask”) tests whether the research process itself can become the work. It asks what a body is, where consciousness comes from, and how the senses compose a world.

featured.title: Singularity
featured.role: Artistic director, creative guide, maker, performer
featured.text: An exhibition-performance built on three years of research (2022–2024). The entire four-storey Piknic building became one structure of consciousness, an eigenvector space for ten collaborating artists, where individual insights meet and break apart at a point of singularity.

featured.title: The Large, the Small, the Mind
featured.venue: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts, S Theater
featured.text: A performance woven from inspirations found in quantum mechanics, neuroscience and astrophysics. A theatre inside a theatre, a closed system within a closed system, where science and art strike sparks off each other.

featured.title: Strange Beauty
featured.venue: Sogeukjang Pan, Seoul · Festival de Spa · Théâtre de Liège
featured.role: Stage concept, set design, research director, director
featured.text: From 2020 to 2022, Belgian and Korean artists observed their own inner landscapes and linked those experiences to the koans of the Gateless Gate. Visual artists, a sound creator, actors, dancers and a video artist each became both maker and performer. Beauty here was not a norm but an event born from the collision of senses.

featured.title: Human Fuga
featured.venue: Namsan Arts Center, Seoul · Bitgoeul Civic Culture Center, Gwangju
featured.text: A stage work based on Han Kang’s novel Human Acts. After a year of travelling to Gwangju for research, the company found its objects in the archive and turned the novel’s text into 35 metaphorical movements. The actors do not play characters; bodies, objects and sound bear witness in the form of a fugue. Named one of the year’s best three by the Korea Theatre Critics’ Association.
